mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, from -52.7% to -30.7% over the last four weeks, indicates an ongoing recovery trend that will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen below 10% (currently 9.4%), it signifies a critical shift in behavior where more people are leaving home, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains below 10% but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in its weekly mean over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined and sustained increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility over the last four weeks suggests a broader return to daily commuting and activity, which will drive increased foot traffic to retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility continue to increase, but RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL (decreasing) mobility indices strongly implies an ongoing easing of public health restrictions, which will continue to positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the observed trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL and increasing WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reverses or stalls significantly (e.g., >5 points week-on-week), then RETAIL_REC will not improve over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The recent significant increase in PARKS mobility from -19.4% to -6.9% (t-1w to t-0w) suggests a growing comfort with outdoor activities, which often precedes or coincides with increased engagement in other leisure activities, boosting RETAIL_REC in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and strong recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, reaching -9.9% (less negative than -10%), indicates a return to more regular out-of-home activity, which will spill over into RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is less negative than -10%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains less negative than -10%, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite recent improvements, if RESIDENTIAL mobility were to unexpectedly increase by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week, it would signal a return to staying home, negatively impacting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC continues to improve or stays stable over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and sustained recovery across RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, and WORKPLACES mobility indices over the last four weeks demonstrates strong underlying momentum for economic reopening, which will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Any of RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, or WORKPLACES show a significant decline (e.g., >5 percentage points week-on-week) in the next four weeks, leading to a flat or negative RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days.
